runs.content: Friday's rotation focus is Lightfin + Games + Cooking + Sports Betting + Work. Since the last thinker run (2026-09-10), log.md shows only one new entry: a routine Cooking recipe-recommender run (3 suggestions for week of 2026-09-14 — Nasi Goreng, a Fuku-style Nashville hot chicken sandwich, Wild Mushrooms on Toast — drawing on the same three chefs, Bourdain/Chang/Slater, already fully covered in the wiki). Checked raw/lightfin, raw/games, raw/sports-betting, and raw/work for any files newer than the last thinker output — none found; all four folders are unchanged since the prior Friday sweep on 2026-09-04. games/prototypes.md and sports-betting/markets.md remain the exact same unpopulated placeholder tables they've been since 2026-05-01. Read work/overview.md and work/source-workday-disruption-debate-2026.md in full to check an apparent mismatch (overview.md names five debate perspectives — Schmidt/Otter/Lettink/Gouvernel/Turnbull — while memory's Domain Content Status only mentions three); this turned out to be a false lead, not a gap: LaRocque's own piece (Source 2) already synthesizes all five names within its 'Where the Debate Gets It Right' section, so nothing is actually missing. Also checked whether Deel — named twice in the Workday debate source page as 'the more interesting bet' for who disrupts HR software — has any Finance presence; it doesn't, but Deel is a private company with no public investment vehicle, so this doesn't clear the bar as a concrete, actionable idea. No investigation idea or cross-domain connection cleared the bar today. Nothing in the existing open sections showed clear signs of resolution — GAW still has no Finance idea page, Eat a Peach still isn't in Books, the WDAY short-research gap is still open, and both Games/Sports Betting stub tables are still empty.

Thursday's rotation focus is Books + Podcasts. Since the last thinker run (2026-09-09), log.md shows a full index.md audit (a separate task, not this one) that resolved both previously-open thinker findings — the Koerner podcast page and a batch of ~29 missing index rows — plus today's routine podcast-recommender run (4 new suggestions: Big Technology Podcast, The Chopping Block, The Price of Football, The Double Pivot). Books had nothing new (book-recommender isn't due until the 15th, book-summarizer not until the 1st). Deep-reading the four new podcast recommendations' own 'Why for Fred' rationale against the Books and Podcasts domain pages, plus a check of Sports Betting and Finance for anything the recommendations might bridge, surfaced one genuinely new, non-duplicate cross-domain connection: The Price of Football (Kevin Day & Kieran Maguire) is pitched explicitly as applying forensic club-accounting rigor — FFP breaches, points deductions, parent-company debt — to football, but sports-betting/markets.md's own Market Types table (1X2, Asian handicap, over/under goals) still reads 'Typical Edge Source: To research' across every row, with zero concept anywhere in the domain of off-pitch financial distress as a betting-relevant signal, even though a points deduction is a discrete, dated event that mechanically moves exactly those markets. Finance's own Hindenburg-style short-selling framework (concept-short-selling.md) is the ready-made toolkit for spotting a breach coming before it lands, but has only ever been pointed at equities, never at a sports subject. None of the three pages (the podcast suggestion, markets.md, concept-short-selling.md) currently cites either of the other two. No new investigation idea cleared the bar today — checked the other three new podcast recommendations (Big Technology, The Chopping Block, The Double Pivot) against ai-future-of-work.md, crypto-overview.md, and the sports-betting domain, but each landed on ground already covered by existing open threads (the institutional-gap/AI-labour-market territory Exponential View already fills, the AI/DeFi circular-financing theme already extensively logged, and the same 'sports podcast keeps getting recommended, domain doesn't move' pattern flagged 4x since June).
